findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on I/O fallible result
findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (missing file, permissions, disk full) panics the caller instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return a Result<Vec<Record>, SessionLoadError> and propagate fs::read_to_string errors with map_err into a domain-typed error such as Io

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on parse fallible result
findings.failure_mode: Any non-numeric content in the second field panics instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: Replace with parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue)? or a domain-typed equivalent

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy as cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: Values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range, producing incorrect data without any error signal
findings.fix: Use u32::try_into().map_err(|_| OverflowError::ValueTooLarge) or parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>().unwrap() (though unwrap also needs fixing)

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec produced by split
findings.failure_mode: An empty line or a line with zero commas produces an empty Vec; parts[0] panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') which returns Option<(&str, &str)> and handle None as a ParseError

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into Vec produced by split
findings.failure_mode: A line with exactly one comma but no second field (or fewer than two fields total) panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and destructure the Option tuple; the second field becomes an &str already bound by the Option

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — side-effecting I/O inside a data-parsing function
findings.failure_mode: The functional core has a hidden logging side effect; makes the function non-deterministic, untestable, and pollutes stdout with internal implementation details
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell layer that calls this function, using a logging facade or explicit callback

findings.problem: println! inside load_sessions violates functional-core/imperative-shell split
findings.failure_mode: Core logic (parsing) should be pure and side-effect-free; hidden I/O prevents pure testing and introduces uncontrolled output
findings.fix: Delete the println!; any session-load logging belongs in the shell caller, not in the pure data-loading core

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() — collects all split parts into Vec<String> unnecessarily
findings.failure_mode: For a two-field record this allocates a Vec<String> with heap allocations for every line; wastes memory and prevents zero-copy parsing
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (&str, &str) directly, avoiding Vec allocation and cloning entirely

findings.problem: pub fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Vec<Record> — no Result wrapper, no error taxonomy
findings.failure_mode: All failure modes (IO, parse, overflow, missing fields) are silenced into potential panics; callers cannot distinguish or handle errors
findings.fix: Define a SessionLoadError enum (Io, Parse, Overflow, Malformed) and return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionLoadError>

findings.problem: Parsing to u32 then casting as u16 instead of parsing or converting with checked arithmetic
findings.failure_mode: Lossy as cast silently truncates values >= 65536; Holzman requires try_from/try_into for all width-down conversions
findings.fix: Use parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(...)? or parse as u32 then u32::try_into().map_err(...)? for checked narrowing

residual_risk: The crate has no error handling whatsoever: every filesystem error, parse error, bounds violation, and overflow is a panic. There is no Result type, no domain error enum, no benchmarks, no tests, and no binary entrypoint. The function mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println!) with data parsing in a single function, violating functional-core/imperative-shell separation. Without repair of all ten blocker findings, this code cannot be considered Holzman-compliant.
